turns.input: *He asks Bartolomhew who they think he is and where he comes from.*
turns.narration:
Bartolomhew's paternal smile doesn't waver, though his pale eyes assess Nicco with calm professional attention. "If I may guess from what I see," he says, his warm voice carrying the practiced cadence of a man accustomed to sizing up strangers, "you carry yourself like someone new to Calderan's streets. The tower behind you—Heartstone—I've never seen its door open before today. Someone appearing there without escort or courier's livery..." He lets the observation hang, then inclines his head slightly. "As for where you come from, that I cannot say. Your speech carries no district accent I recognize."

He folds his hands before him, the gesture somewhere between clerical and mercantile. "But you asked who I think you are. A man with questions rather than answers, for one. That marks you as either cautious or uninformed—and in my experience, the two often walk together." His smile widened fractionally, reaching nowhere near his eyes. "I am Bartolomhew. I deal in labor contracts and relocation of willing workers, among other arrangements. You have the look of someone who might need trustworthy hands, or perhaps has goods to move. Heartstone's size suggests both possibilities."

[CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE ACCESS]
Facts: F1 campaign_fact_nicco_light_mage "Nicco is a Light mage." | F2 campaign_fact_nicco_otherworlder "Nicco came to this world from another world." | H1 household "Nicco is owner of the household Heartstone."
Narration and Nicco (player): F1, F2, H1. Nicco's speech and decisions still belong to the player.
Bartolomhew: CAN USE none; DO NOT USE F1, F2, H1
A character may voice or act on only the facts listed CAN USE for them (believes/suspects/heard_rumor: only as belief, suspicion or rumor). DO NOT USE also covers hints, rumors, "everyone says" talk and claims that imply the fact; do not invent rumors or public talk to get around it. DO NOT USE is this turn's permission, not proof of ignorance: that character may ask, say they have not heard, or defer to someone who can use it.
UNKNOWN IS NOT A RUMOR: when a character cannot use a fact, it is unknown to them, never something they heard. "People say", "I heard", "word is", "everyone knows", registries, records, reports, past meetings or sightings are sources; a character may cite one only when a CAN USE entry with that basis exists. Allowed instead: "I don't know", a question, or a guess explicitly framed as a guess and based only on what they can see or hear right now.
